home.hero.title: Combine uncertain evidence.
home.hero.body: Compare Dempster-Shafer and DSmT fusion methods side by side. Inspect how conflict is handled. Run classifier ensembles through the same pipeline.

home.step3.title: Fuse
home.step3.detail: Run the combination rule to merge all sources into a single belief distribution.

home.methods.label: Fusion methods
home.methods.title: DST vs DSmT at a glance
home.dst.title: Dempster-Shafer
home.dst.body: Normalises conflict into the fused masses. Strong when sources broadly agree and conflict is low. The classic choice for most evidence fusion workflows.
home.pcr.title: PCR5 / PCR6
home.pcr.body: Redistributes conflict back to focal elements proportionally. Better when disagreement between sources is meaningful and you want to preserve nuance.
home.cta2.title: New to evidence fusion?
home.cta2.body: Start with a guided example. See fusion in action before building your own inputs.

method.category.normalized.title: Normalized result
method.category.normalized.body: Conflict is removed from the empty set and the remaining masses are rescaled.
method.category.redistribution.title: Conflict redistribution
method.category.redistribution.body: Conflict is moved back to the focal propositions that created it.
method.category.union_transfer.title: Union transfer
method.category.union_transfer.body: Conflicting mass is assigned to proposition unions such as A ∪ B.
method.category.ignorance_transfer.title: Ignorance transfer
method.category.ignorance_transfer.body: Conflict becomes total ignorance instead of a single winning hypothesis.
method.category.open_conflict.title: Open conflict
method.category.open_conflict.body: The result may contain ∅, the empty set, so unresolved conflict stays visible.

ml.method.category.advanced.title: Advanced: uncertainty and conflict
ml.method.category.advanced.body: Useful when you want to inspect indecision, ignorance, or unions of classes instead of only one label.
ml.method.category.diagnostic.title: Diagnostic / academic

docs.title: Documentation
docs.intro: Fusion Lab combines belief functions from multiple sources using classical and DSmT rules, and lets you compare sklearn classifiers fused via the same machinery.
docs.dst.title: Dempster–Shafer (DST)
docs.dst.body: Conflict is normalized into the combined masses. Use when sources are mostly consistent and you want the standard normalized rule.
docs.pcr.title: PCR5 and PCR6
docs.pcr.body: Conflict is redistributed to focal elements (proportionally; PCR6 refines the case of three or more sources). Prefer when disagreement is informative and should not be only normalized away.
docs.ml.title: ML pipeline
docs.ml.body: Models output class probabilities, converted to belief assignments on singletons, then fused per test sample. Metrics and sample-level analysis compare fusion to the best single model and to majority vote.
result.chart.title: Fused masses
result.empty.explain: is the empty set. It represents unresolved contradiction between mutually exclusive hypotheses, not a normal hypothesis.
conflict.panel.title: Conflict between sources
conflict.panel.subtitle: Pairwise conflict — the mass each pair assigns to mutually exclusive hypotheses. Higher values mean stronger disagreement.
